title: Reduce classical conditional-Umegaki comparison to finite noncommuting inverse forms
statement: For finite column-stochastic K,L with common n-input alphabet and m_K,m_L nonzero output rows, define J_K=D(Krho||Ksigma)-D(rho_R||sigma_R), only with finite terms. For Q_i>0 summing to I and complex zero-sum u_i, let W_y=sum_i k_yi Q_i, v_y=sum_i k_yi u_i and F_K=sum_y v_y* W_y^-1 v_y. The conditional/equal-reference coefficient is sup F_K/F_L in active dimensions<=n-1+m_K+m_L; reference dimension<=n+m_K+m_L suffices. Rational-channel finite coefficients are algebraic and rational threshold comparison is decidable in principle.

requires: Both channels share an explicit finite classical input/dephasing boundary; arbitrary finite quantum references. Delete zero output rows. A positive numerator with zero denominator forbids any finite coefficient; 0/0 imposes no condition. Limits need not attain an optimizer. Compare all priors, not a prescribed baseline.

body: Normalize conditional BKM superoperators and use u_i=a_i-Q_i sum(a_j), which simultaneously gauges away the marginal tangent for K,L. Span the zero-sum vectors and both sets of inverse-applied output vectors: dimension<=n-1+m_K+m_L, with exact preservation of both forms. Lift each witness to sigma_i=(1-epsilon)Q_i/d direct_sum epsilon*p_i and offdiagonal H_i=[0,u_i;u_i*,0]. Sum H_i=0, a Schur radius ensures positivity, and the BKM metric divided by2d log(1/epsilon) tends to F_K. Hessian/path integration gives the coefficient equality; a fixed-c violation handles zero denominators and singular suprema. Rational coordinates, positivity and inverse variables give a semialgebraic threshold ray with algebraic finite endpoint. Equality itself is earlier N965; binary specialization is earlier N970.
